newsitem.title: NIGERIA: Shell says 88 staff still held in Nigerian protest.
newsitem.headline: Shell says 88 staff still held in Nigerian protest.

text.p: Eighty-eight staff of oil giant Royal Dutch/Shell were still been held hostage on Wednesday by Nigerians protesting against the relocation of their local government headquarters, a company spokesman said.
"The overall situation remains unchanged," said the spokesman in Lagos.

"Apart from those we told you about earlier it has come to our knowledge that nine of the people detained left on Saturday and Monday by their own methods so 88 are now being held," the spokesman said in Lagos.
All the staff involved are Nigerians.
Local newspapers reported on Wednesday that three Ijaw tribesmen were killed in protests in the oil town of Warri on Tuesday in an escalation of the crisis which has shut six Shell oil flow stations.
Riot police are patrolling the town, which is the western operational headquarters from Shell. Several other oil companies also have offices in Warri.
Shell says despite reducing Nigeria's crude oil output by 100,000 barrels per day, the crisis has not affected exports.
"Exports continue to be as normal. They are not affected by the dispute," said the Shell spokesman in Lagos.
He said community leaders had met state officials and Shell was hopeful that this could lead to the release of its staff.
"At least dialogue has been established," he said.
A Shell boat which went to the sites occupied by villagers on Tuesday evacuated 12 men, six with injuries though not seriously, he added.
"We, however, remain concerned about one seriously injured person who was not allowed to leave," he said.
Communal clashes are common in Nigeria's impoverished oil-producing areas where the African nation derives more than 90 percent of its export revenue.
The latest crisis, which began last Saturday, does not directly involve Shell but the oil giant is caught in it because of its high profile in Nigeria and huge operations in Warri.
